html:
The Yawarawarka are an Aboriginal people of the channel country near Cooper Creek, on the border of South Australia and Queensland, in the far northeast corner of South Australia.

Their neighbours on the map include the Yandruwandha, the Diyari and the Wangkumara. The peoples of this region shared trade routes, ceremonies and ways of life built around the waterholes of the Cooper, which fill after rain far to the north. In 1861 the explorers of the Burke and Wills expedition died on the Cooper, not far away. Little is recorded about the Yawarawarka as a separate group. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Yawarawarka are an Aboriginal people of the channel country near Cooper Creek, on the border of South Australia and Queensland, in the far northeast corner of South Australia.
